notes: Measurement started 2026-10-26T23:09:09.975551Z and finished 2026-10-27T00:54:36.211032Z; date is the UTC start day. Unmodified main c7cf2c4436bc045ac9993c0bd99eca377fb64882, cargo release profile; system Git only, no baseline grit release. Each executable `grit-bench daily --list` scenario was invoked sequentially with `daily --only <id> --output <path>` using explicit release grit and system git paths. The runner aborts on a scenario error, so isolated invocations preserve failures and allow the full matrix to complete. No other heavy jobs ran during measurements. The unchanged runner uses one warmup per tool, then adaptive alternating git/grit samples (3–20 runs/tool, approximately 3 seconds combined timed duration, 120-second sampling budget), measures per-command peak RSS via its direct-spawn helper, and performs a separate untimed traced run per tool. Published fields rename median_wall_ms to median_ms and convert peak_rss_bytes to max_rss_kb by dividing by 1024; original sample statistics and whole detail objects are preserved for initial-only scenarios. Functional area names are mapped to the requested public schema. Headline flags/names are carried from the registry, including its additional headline scenarios. Noise check compared initial ratios against the previous published 2026-10-25 report (which used system Git 2.43.0, versus 2.55.0 today); thresholds are >20% worse time ratio or >30% worse RSS ratio. 26 scenarios were rerun three additional times: add/modified@synth-10k, commit/small@synth-10k, fetch/incremental@git-git, pull/fast-forward@git-git, pull/rebase@synth-10k, push/force-with-lease@git-git, push/incremental@git-git, add/modified@big-blobs, branch/delete@many-refs, clone/bare@synth-10k, commit/paths@synth-10k, commit/small@small, commit/small@synth-100k, commit/staged@synth-100k, fetch/dry-run@git-git, fetch/incremental-http@git-git, fetch/noop@git-git, fetch/one-branch@git-git, patch-id/commit@git-git, pull/check@git-git, push/incremental-http@git-git, remote/remove@many-refs, shortlog/ahead@git-git, stash/list@synth-10k, status/paths@synth-100k, switch/branch@synth-100k. For rerun scenarios median_ms and stddev_ms use all concatenated successful timed samples, runs is their count, min/max span all invocation statistics, and max_rss_kb is the maximum observed peak across invocations. Original first-pass detail objects remain unchanged; their phases come from that pass. 10 scenarios reported failures: add/hunks@large-file, add/lines@large-file, add/patch-file@large-file, clone/shallow@git-git, fetch/deepen@git-git, history/reword@synth-10k, push/refspec@git-git, remote/rename@many-refs, resolve/change-id@git-git, revs/count-path@git-git. No-op placeholder plans (recorded command true) are retained as failures with null measurements, never counted as operation timings; their original detail objects are preserved. No source changes, test changes, or main integration were made. Repository metadata was recounted after measurement: files at the fixture baseline, commits reachable from all refs, total refs, and pack_mb from .pack bytes divided by 1024 squared. Standard shapes use canonical caches; special shapes use the measured scratch fixture. The large-file metadata is derived from the recounted synth-10k base plus the one committed file added by the runner. Individual variants and resets are defined by the unmodified runner and detail.prepare commands.
